```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message =FALSE)
```

Let's finish our study of the career of Serena Williams. First, let's attach the packages we need: 

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
```

Second, let's create one of the tables we've created in Exercise 02, namely the table with the breakdown of the finals won and lost by Serena on the different tournaments. Remember that the process started with generating the dataset `serena_finals_data`.

```{r}
serena_finals_data  <-
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gruggeri/tennis_wta/master/wta_grand_slam_data.csv" %>% 
  read_csv(col_types = cols(.default = "c")) %>% 
  select(year, winner_name,loser_name, tourney_name,round) %>% 
  filter(
    winner_name == "Serena Williams" | loser_name == "Serena Williams",
    round=="F"
    ) %>% 
  mutate(year = as.numeric(year))
```

Now, let's create the breakdown!


```{r}
serena_finals_per_champ <- serena_finals_data %>% 
  mutate(
    won_or_lost = 
      case_when(
        winner_name == "Serena Williams" ~ "Serena Won! :)",
        loser_name == "Serena Williams" ~ "Serena Lost! :("
        )
    ) %>% 
  group_by(tourney_name, won_or_lost) %>% 
  summarise(number_of_championships = n()) %>% 
  ungroup()

serena_finals_per_champ
```

This table does not look very good for reporting, right? It would be more appealing to display the single name of the championship in the rows, and the number of won / lost finals two columns!

Use the right verb with the right arguments to do that!

```{r}
serena_finals_per_champ %>% 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = won_or_lost, 
    values_from = number_of_championships) %>% 
  rename(`Tourney Name`) %>% 
  knitr::kable()
```
